title: Trump’s Great Oil Heist
gist: Cristina Ramirez argues that after the US ousted Nicolás Maduro, Venezuela's hopes for democratic transition are fading as Washington works to control the country's oil wealth; billions in US and foreign investment could entrench the chavista regime and give future US presidents incentives to preserve the political status quo.

insights.claim: Venezuela's hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth.
insights.speaker: CRISTINA RAMIREZ
insights.so_what: US-led access to Venezuelan crude may expand supply, but political legitimacy risk hangs over the investments.
insights.quote: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth.
insights.locator: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition

insights.claim: Billions in US and foreign investment in Venezuelan oil could strengthen the chavista regime and give future American presidents powerful incentives to preserve the political status quo.
insights.speaker: CRISTINA RAMIREZ
insights.so_what: Investor capital in Venezuelan oil becomes a stake in regime continuity, aligning US policy with stability over democratization.
insights.quote: Billions in US and foreign investment could strengthen the chavista regime
insights.locator: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition

insights.claim: The US ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro earlier this year and jailed him in New York, giving Venezuela its first real possibility of regime change in 27 years.
insights.speaker: CRISTINA RAMIREZ
insights.so_what: Marks a major geopolitical shift in Venezuela with implications for oil-sector reopening.
insights.quote: For the first time in 27 years, the country faced a real possibility of regime change.
